methodology: Criteria authored from canonical paper text, TOC and equations before generating candidates. Node IDs are TOC ordinals, rebound and page-validated by the runner. The parsed equation text is imperfect; visual equation fidelity requires the original figure/page and human review.

cases.question: Why does scaled dot-product attention divide the query-key dot products by the square root of the key dimension?

coverage_points: Larger key dimensions can increase the magnitude of unscaled query-key dot products.
Large logits push softmax toward regions with very small gradients.
Dividing by sqrt(d_k) counters this effect before softmax; do not confuse it with scaling the values.
The independent-component illustration gives dot-product variance d_k and is an assumption, not a universal data guarantee.

cases.question: Summarize this entire paper, including the architecture, attention equation, position information, training, main results and limitations. Cite the original sections and pages.

coverage_points: Describe the encoder-decoder architecture, self-attention, decoder masking and encoder-decoder attention.
Explain Attention(Q,K,V)=softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d_k))V and parallel projected attention heads.
Explain why position information is needed and how sinusoidal and learned encodings were compared.
Discuss parallelism, path lengths and complexity tradeoffs without claiming attention is always cheaper.
Cover training data, optimization schedule, regularization and reported experimental conditions.
Report the big model's 28.4 English-German and 41.0 English-French BLEU with the correct tasks and qualification.
Include model variations, constituency parsing and the conclusion's future directions; separate reported findings from hypotheses or later Transformer developments.
